title: Require HTTPS on public routes
check: Review configured production listeners and recorded public responses for a trusted certificate and an HTTP redirect.
remediation: Terminate TLS at the public edge and use a redirect for public HTTP traffic.

title: Set Secure on session cookies
check: Check the production session configuration for Secure on session and remember-me cookies.
remediation: Require HTTPS for the cookie at the application and proxy boundaries.

title: Keep authentication cookies unreadable to scripts
check: Check the configuration for HttpOnly on cookies that contain authentication state.
remediation: Limit script-readable cookies to state the browser needs directly.

title: Set an intentional SameSite policy
check: Review the intended cross-site sign-in and callback flows against the cookie SameSite configuration.
remediation: Set the narrowest compatible policy and document any cross-site exception.

title: Enforce authorization where data changes
check: Locate the server-side authorization check beside the application action that reads or modifies protected records.
remediation: Enforce permissions at the operation boundary and cover allow and deny cases in owned tests.

title: Scope records to their owning tenant
check: Review record lookups and update operations for a tenant or ownership predicate.
remediation: Apply one consistent ownership rule and test it with separate tenant fixtures.

title: Refresh the session after authentication
check: Review the sign-in flow for session regeneration after credentials are accepted.
remediation: Regenerate the session at sign-in and privilege changes.

title: Revoke sessions after account recovery
check: Check whether account recovery invalidates old sessions and remembered authentication state.
remediation: Revoke stale session and remember-token credentials after a password reset.

title: Protect browser-initiated state changes
check: Review framework CSRF middleware and exceptions for authenticated browser forms that modify state.
remediation: Use the framework's CSRF protection and scope exceptions to verified non-browser callbacks.

title: Reserve GET for read-only behavior
check: Review route definitions and their handlers for writes behind read-only methods.
remediation: Move mutations to methods intended for changes and require the appropriate authorization.

title: Review installed dependency versions
check: Match resolved package versions in committed lockfiles against published vendor or ecosystem advisories.
remediation: Upgrade affected dependencies to supported versions and verify applicable paths.

title: Keep production debugging private
check: Review deployment configuration and ordinary production error responses for diagnostic details.
remediation: Disable public debug rendering and keep diagnostics in restricted logs.

title: Load private credentials from secret storage
check: Review configuration for literal secrets and verify that runtime credential references are managed by the owner.
remediation: Move credentials to secret storage and rotate any affected credential.

title: Limit deployment permissions
check: Review who and what can deploy to each environment and what those identities can change.
remediation: Use a dedicated deployment identity scoped to the necessary resources.

title: Set deliberate content-type handling
check: Review the response configuration for accurate content types and MIME sniffing protection.
remediation: Send the correct media type and apply X-Content-Type-Options where supported.

title: Define which sites can frame the page
check: Review the configured framing policy against documented embedding requirements.
remediation: Set a frame-ancestors policy matching the approved embedding use cases.

title: Keep content within the viewport
check: Review the same page at desktop and narrow widths and record unintended horizontal overflow.
remediation: Let containers and content reflow with widths that can shrink.

title: Prevent avoidable layout jumps
check: Record whether delayed media or controls shift visible content in a normal loading sequence.
remediation: Reserve layout space for media and asynchronous sections.

title: Make truncated information recoverable
check: Review long labels and values in constrained cards for an accessible way to read the full text.
remediation: Wrap important content or provide an explicit way to reveal it.

title: Support enlarged text
check: Review core screens with enlarged text and note where controls overlap or content disappears.
remediation: Use flexible sizing and allow text containers to expand or wrap.

title: Space touch controls adequately
check: Measure primary touch controls and their spacing at a narrow viewport.
remediation: Increase interactive area or spacing without changing the visual meaning.

title: Keep sticky controls from covering content
check: Review sticky regions and locate any important content or focus position they obscure.
remediation: Reserve space for sticky regions and ensure relevant content remains visible.

title: Make status contrast legible
check: Measure status text and icons against their actual backgrounds, including dark mode.
remediation: Update semantic colors to maintain usable contrast in each theme.

title: Make disabled controls recognizable
check: Compare actionable and disabled controls and review how the reason is communicated.
remediation: Pair the visual state with a clear disabled behavior and relevant explanation.

title: Use consistent visual hierarchy
check: Check that grouped content and its primary action can be distinguished without relying on color alone.
remediation: Align headings, labels, spacing, and action styles with the shared component hierarchy.

title: Give empty states useful structure
check: Review first-use, filtered-empty, and permission-limited screens for an appropriate next action.
remediation: Provide a short description and the action that can change each state.

title: Keep loading states stable
check: Review ordinary slow-loading local fixtures for jumps, ambiguous spinners, or duplicate controls.
remediation: Reserve suitable space and show a loading state tied to the pending work.

title: Keep shared component variants consistent
check: Compare the same control in its ordinary, focused, busy, disabled, and error states.
remediation: Use a common component and semantic state styling.

title: Fit dialogs to the available viewport
check: Review dialogs at narrow widths and verify that their content and actions remain reachable.
remediation: Constrain the dialog to the viewport and allow its content region to scroll.

title: Keep dense tables usable
check: Review a table with realistic column lengths and data density at narrow widths.
remediation: Preserve column meanings with a usable scroll region or a suitable small-screen representation.

title: Honor reduced motion preferences
check: Review animated navigation and status transitions with reduced motion enabled.
remediation: Disable nonessential movement while keeping the same content and actions available.

title: Communicate state without color alone
check: Check whether success, error, and selection states are understandable without hue.
remediation: Combine color with visible text, shape, or an accessible state announcement.

title: Complete core journeys with a keyboard
check: Complete the ordinary journey on an owned fixture using keyboard input and record any unreachable control.
remediation: Use keyboard-operable controls and preserve predictable movement between them.

title: Show keyboard focus clearly
check: Review the focus indicator for interactive fields, links, buttons, and composite controls.
remediation: Use a visible focus indicator that remains discernible in every theme.

title: Return focus from transient interfaces
check: Open and close a dialog or menu on an owned fixture and note where focus lands.
remediation: Restore focus to the trigger or a meaningful nearby control.

title: Give every control a meaningful label
check: Review accessible names for controls with placeholders, symbols, or image-only content.
remediation: Connect a visible label or appropriate accessible name to each control.

title: Use headings that reflect content structure
check: Review the page heading hierarchy and landmark names using available accessibility evidence.
remediation: Use meaningful headings and landmarks that reflect the page structure.

title: Help users recover from form errors
check: Review whether existing field values and specific error locations remain clear after ordinary fixture validation.
remediation: Keep valid input and identify each field and correction in accessible text.

title: Confirm long-running submissions
check: Review an owned fixture submission for a visible pending state and a meaningful result.
remediation: Show that work is in progress and communicate completion or recovery.

title: Name the effect of destructive actions
check: Review destructive controls and confirmations for an explicit object and effect.
remediation: Use precise confirmation language and offer recovery when feasible.

title: Distinguish empty results from errors
check: Compare no-data fixtures with failed-loading fixtures and record the available actions.
remediation: Give each state a distinct message and relevant action.

title: Make current filters visible
check: Review filtered pages for a visible applied state, result total, and clear-reset action.
remediation: Expose the current filter selection and make clearing it straightforward.

title: Restore useful navigation state
check: Review normal history navigation for pages selected through tabs, filters, or pagination.
remediation: Store shareable state in the URL and restore it on history navigation.

title: Show advanced fields when needed
check: Review whether required inputs are clear before users encounter optional complexity.
remediation: Keep required inputs prominent and group advanced options separately.

title: Announce asynchronous results
check: Review loading and result states for meaningful assistive-technology updates.
remediation: Use a suitable live status for actionable changes without interrupting the current task.

title: Offer an explicit cancel path
check: Review a long-running operation for a discoverable cancellation or dismissal action.
remediation: Provide a consistent cancel action and communicate the operation's resulting state.

title: Keep translated journeys complete
check: Review an entire journey in a supported alternate language for untranslated text or clipped labels.
remediation: Use shared translations and check navigation, validation, and confirmation text.

title: Describe meaningful images
check: Review whether content images and image controls have an appropriate accessible alternative.
remediation: Give meaningful images descriptive alternatives and mark decorative images appropriately.

title: Set a representative navigation budget
check: Collect ordinary local or staging timing samples using documented conditions and compare them with a target.
remediation: Set a repeatable budget based on representative users and track changes.

title: Keep initial transfer sizes bounded
check: Compare observed transfer sizes for the initial page against the assets needed above the fold.
remediation: Defer nonessential resources and compress or resize heavy payloads.

title: Deliver images sized for their use
check: Compare displayed image dimensions with the assets supplied to representative devices.
remediation: Deliver responsive image variants sized for the displayed context.

title: Prioritize resources needed for first render
check: Review the ordinary page waterfall and identify first-render resources waiting on unrelated work.
remediation: Load critical styles and primary media first and defer secondary modules.

title: Limit render-blocking scripts
check: Review which JavaScript resources delay usable content during an ordinary load.
remediation: Defer nonessential scripts and keep blocking work small.

title: Set a route bundle-size budget
check: Review built asset sizes by route, including shared code loaded before any interaction.
remediation: Split optional features and enforce a build budget where supported.

title: Keep interaction work bounded
check: Observe representative interactions and record long browser main-thread work.
remediation: Move infrequent work off the critical path or break it into shorter tasks.

title: Keep large result lists responsive
check: Use owned fixtures with known list sizes and compare initial rendering and scrolling.
remediation: Paginate or virtualize result lists when the visible portion is much smaller than the dataset.

title: Cancel obsolete client work
check: Review rapid navigation or filter changes for requests or callbacks that continue after the current view changes.
remediation: Abort stale requests and ignore callbacks for superseded view state.

title: Set cache policies by resource type
check: Review ordinary response headers for immutable assets and stateful or personalized responses.
remediation: Cache versioned static assets and use appropriate policy for personalized content.

title: Cache stable repeated reads deliberately
check: Review ordinary traces for repeated expensive reads that can tolerate freshness limits.
remediation: Cache suitable results with an explicit expiry and invalidation plan.

title: Batch independent data lookups
check: Review traces for sequential reads whose dependencies do not require ordering.
remediation: Batch eligible reads while preserving request limits and error handling.

title: Bound export work and memory use
check: Review export logic for unbounded materialization and synchronous response deadlines.
remediation: Stream large output or run it in a queue with a controlled artifact lifecycle.

title: Load only needed font assets
check: Review font resources for unused weights and a visible fallback during normal loading.
remediation: Subset or reduce fonts and use a deliberate font-display strategy.

title: Measure the cost of third-party resources
check: Identify scripts and media from outside the application that affect initial loading in staging.
remediation: Defer or remove integrations whose cost exceeds their value for the user journey.

title: Measure service memory under expected work
check: Observe representative owned staging traffic and record stable memory and restart behavior.
remediation: Bound the workload or cache and size the service from repeatable observations.

title: Enforce domain invariants in the service layer
check: Review whether business rules apply consistently across HTTP, job, and CLI callers.
remediation: Put critical invariants in a shared service or domain boundary.

title: Return actionable validation errors
check: Check expected invalid fixture values for an appropriate response and specific error fields.
remediation: Use boundary validation and keep machine-readable errors stable.

title: Keep related state changes atomic
check: Review multi-record application actions for partial writes after an expected failure.
remediation: Use a transaction or explicit compensation and verify persisted outcomes.

title: Protect updates from lost writes
check: Review competing updates to the same record using two owned test transactions.
remediation: Use appropriate locks, version checks, or atomic updates for contested data.

title: Represent time and timezone intentionally
check: Review expiry, scheduling, and reporting code for conversion or boundary ambiguity.
remediation: Store unambiguous instants and localize presentation at defined edges.

title: Make monetary rounding explicit
check: Review billing or reconciliation rules for precision and rounding order using approved fixtures.
remediation: Use fixed precision and document the business rounding policy.

title: Classify recoverable and permanent failures
check: Review exception handlers for an intentional distinction between retryable and terminal errors.
remediation: Map known conditions explicitly and report unexpected faults consistently.

title: Coordinate external effects after state commits
check: Review messages, jobs, and downstream calls that can run before a transaction commits.
remediation: Use after-commit dispatch or an outbox with clear delivery guarantees.

title: Make repeated job deliveries harmless
check: Review ordinary worker redelivery using an owned fixture and compare recorded side effects.
remediation: Use a stable idempotency key and persist the outcome at the right boundary.

title: Normalize inputs at a clear boundary
check: Review text, numeric, and date conversions for inconsistent rules across callers.
remediation: Define one normalization policy before the data enters the domain logic.

title: Enforce valid state transitions
check: Check that terminal, pending, and reversal transitions have clear rules and tests.
remediation: Use explicit transition logic and reject invalid or duplicate transitions.

title: Define outcomes for partial bulk failures
check: Review bulk operations with a fixture that contains a mix of valid and invalid items.
remediation: Make atomic or partial-success behavior explicit and identify failed items.

title: Keep paging order deterministic
check: Review database ordering when multiple rows share the displayed sort field.
remediation: Add a stable unique tie-breaker and carry it through cursor pagination.

title: Bound large application reads
check: Review server handlers for unbounded collection loads as dataset size increases.
remediation: Paginate or stream suitable data and set maximum result sizes.

title: Release resources after a worker task
check: Review job processing paths for cleanup on completion, failure, and cancellation.
remediation: Close temporary resources and reset per-job state reliably.

title: Validate required runtime configuration
check: Review how missing required configuration fails at startup or first use.
remediation: Check required values early and report the missing field without logging its secret.

title: Keep schema changes compatible during rollout
check: Review whether current and previous application releases can safely access the migration's intermediate schema.
remediation: Add compatible structures first and remove retired structures in a later release.

title: Review migration lock and rewrite impact
check: Check database-specific documentation and staging timing for schema changes on large tables.
remediation: Choose a staged or online change appropriate to the database and table size.

title: Make backfills resumable and measurable
check: Review backfill logic for bounded batches, progress tracking, and repeatability.
remediation: Write a resumable backfill with checkpoints and validate representative records.

title: Plan how existing rows get required values
check: Review new required columns for a backfill, valid default, or an expansion period.
remediation: Populate existing records before enforcing presence or remove ambiguity with a valid default.

title: Enforce uniqueness where concurrency matters
check: Review database constraints for records that must be unique across concurrent writes.
remediation: Add the appropriate unique constraint and handle duplicate outcomes predictably.

title: Protect relationships with referential constraints
check: Review schema relationships for database constraints or documented alternatives.
remediation: Use appropriate references and decide how deletions affect dependent rows.

title: Match indexes to actual query patterns
check: Inspect an execution plan for a representative query in an owned staging database.
remediation: Test an index matching the observed predicates and ordering before release.

title: Review repeated queries inside loops
check: Review collection loops for per-item lookups and measure query growth with owned fixtures.
remediation: Use joins, preloading, or bounded batches where they preserve semantics.

title: Define how missing values behave
check: Review whether NULL, empty text, and default values are deliberately distinguished.
remediation: Choose explicit nullability and handle missing values consistently.

title: Choose data types for real value ranges
check: Review columns that store quantities, prices, counters, or timestamps for precision and limits.
remediation: Use a type that supports the documented range and preserve precision at boundaries.

title: Document isolation requirements
check: Review transactions for the consistency level expected by their business rules.
remediation: Use appropriate isolation or locking and test concurrent operations with owned fixtures.

title: Handle replica freshness deliberately
check: Review whether immediate reads after a write can go to a lagging replica.
remediation: Use an appropriate consistency path for workflows that require the newest value.

title: Keep database connection counts bounded
check: Review pool settings and observe connection usage during representative staging work.
remediation: Set bounded pools and avoid opening duplicate connections for a single request.

title: Demonstrate restores on an owned environment
check: Review the recorded restore exercise, recovery time, and recovered data checks.
remediation: Schedule restoration drills with an isolated target and validate recovered records.

title: Keep cleanup operations traceable
check: Review retention jobs for scope limits, predictable deletion order, and audited outcomes.
remediation: Use bounded cleanup batches and record what policy produced each result.

title: Set limits for long-running database work
check: Review connection and statement deadlines against request and background-job deadlines.
remediation: Choose bounded query timeouts based on workload and database capabilities.

title: Set deadlines for outbound dependencies
check: Review critical dependency calls for an explicit timeout within the overall request budget.
remediation: Apply both connection and operation deadlines and handle expiry clearly.

title: Retry only eligible transient failures
check: Review retry policies for eligible errors, maximum attempts, and total duration.
remediation: Limit retries to transient conditions and apply backoff with jitter.

title: Avoid multiplying retries across layers
check: Compare retry policies at the client, service, queue, and downstream integration.
remediation: Assign retry ownership and budget across the whole request path.

title: Preserve exhausted jobs for review
check: Review how exhausted jobs are quarantined and surfaced to operators.
remediation: Retain metadata for exhausted jobs and define an authorized replay process.

title: Drain work before process shutdown
check: Review a controlled staging shutdown for active requests and leased jobs.
remediation: Stop accepting new work, drain in-flight tasks, and leave retryable work recoverable.

title: Define behavior when a dependency is unavailable
check: Review core journeys when an optional dependency is replaced by a failing owned fixture.
remediation: Keep essential work available or show a clear, recoverable fallback.

title: Limit concurrent work to safe capacity
check: Review the point at which request or job load exceeds downstream capacity.
remediation: Use bounded queues and concurrency controls that preserve service health.

title: Separate readiness from basic process liveness
check: Review what health checks verify before a service starts receiving traffic.
remediation: Keep liveness simple and require essential readiness signals for routing.

title: Identify the state needed for recovery
check: Review critical workflows and identify which state must survive process loss.
remediation: Persist recovery state at reliable boundaries and document recovery order.

title: Align leases with job timeouts
check: Review worker execution deadlines, queue retry intervals, and shutdown grace.
remediation: Set job execution deadlines below the retry lease and validate redelivery behavior.

title: Use explicit defaults for optional dependencies
check: Review whether optional feature configuration fails closed or falls back safely.
remediation: Document a safe default and surface disabled optional functions clearly.

title: Record dependencies without a fallback
check: Review critical journeys for services whose failure stops all progress.
remediation: Document the owner, impact, recovery option, and acceptable outage for each dependency.

title: Maintain an executable recovery runbook
check: Review whether the latest runbook matches a completed owned recovery exercise.
remediation: Update steps, prerequisites, verification, and escalation paths after exercises.

title: Set recovery objectives for critical journeys
check: Determine the maximum acceptable outage and data loss for each important journey.
remediation: Define recovery objectives and verify them through scheduled exercises.

title: Track critical user-facing availability
check: Review whether an availability measure represents completed user actions.
remediation: Monitor meaningful outcomes and use a target agreed with service owners.

title: Prevent conflicting background tasks
check: Review whether concurrent tasks can process the same resource in incompatible ways.
remediation: Use a scoped lock or uniqueness rule for mutually exclusive work.

title: Keep module dependencies directional
check: Review dependency relationships for cycles or internal layers depending on interface code.
remediation: Define stable module boundaries and move shared contracts to a suitable location.

title: Centralize business policy used in multiple paths
check: Review repeated pricing, eligibility, or permission constants for inconsistent updates.
remediation: Move shared policy to an explicit owner and test its callers.

title: Read environment configuration at the boundary
check: Review application code for direct environment reads that change behavior under config caching.
remediation: Expose settings through the framework's configuration layer.

title: Make complex branches explain the decision
check: Review a deeply nested business flow for its branch conditions and expected outcomes.
remediation: Name meaningful decisions and return early where doing so preserves behavior.

title: Remove behavior with no remaining caller
check: Check reachability and usage evidence for old paths identified during the change.
remediation: Remove confirmed obsolete code together with references that would mislead maintainers.

title: Make new dependency purpose visible
check: Review each new dependency for a clear usage site and an owner.
remediation: Reuse existing capabilities where sufficient and keep a dependency only while it serves a clear need.

title: Replace unsupported framework APIs
check: Check the installed runtime and package versions against the APIs used by the change.
remediation: Migrate to supported equivalents and keep the runtime compatibility documented.

title: Use domain terms in public module boundaries
check: Review new handlers and public methods for consistent domain vocabulary.
remediation: Name concepts consistently across routes, services, models, and tests.

title: Keep example settings aligned with application reads
check: Compare configuration keys and defaults against a committed safe example.
remediation: Update the example when settings are added and keep each environment's values out of source.

title: Keep task documentation aligned with the current entry point
check: Use adjacent code and current UI labels to review a maintained procedure.
remediation: Update the exact steps and references affected by the change.

title: Record responsibility for critical modules
check: Review the ownership of frequently changed modules and cross-team interfaces.
remediation: Assign a code owner or an equivalent review path.

title: Give temporary flags a cleanup condition
check: Review rollout flags for an owner, purpose, and removal trigger.
remediation: Document the trigger and remove stale flags once callers converge.

title: Review modules with repeated maintenance churn
check: Use version history and recurring issues to identify the actual boundary under change.
remediation: Extract a stable design only after identifying the repeated cause.

title: Use explicit types at shared boundaries
check: Review data crossing module or service boundaries for implicit meanings and shape shifts.
remediation: Give stable structure and documented meanings to shared inputs and outputs.

title: Keep implementation comments tied to intent
check: Review comments for obsolete behavior or narration already clear from the code.
remediation: Remove stale remarks and explain surprising tradeoffs close to the relevant code.

title: Identify parts that make upgrades difficult
check: Review vendor integration points for custom assumptions that complicate supported upgrades.
remediation: Place version-sensitive behavior behind a small explicit boundary.

title: Maintain a contract for API inputs and outputs
check: Compare implemented endpoint shapes with the maintained schema or integration contract.
remediation: Update the interface and its contract together and test representative responses.

title: Use consistent HTTP result codes
check: Review successful, validation-failed, unauthorized, and unavailable cases on an owned fixture.
remediation: Choose status codes and response bodies that let callers handle the result correctly.

title: Return machine-readable API errors
check: Compare error responses across intended API clients and libraries.
remediation: Use a consistent error format with stable codes and actionable field details.

title: Specify how API pages connect
check: Review cursor invalidation, default sizes, and fields used for API pagination.
remediation: Document cursor semantics and return stable links or continuation tokens.

title: Plan backward compatibility for API changes
check: Review proposed API shape and behavior changes against currently supported clients.
remediation: Use a compatibility window, versioned contract, or staged consumer migration.

title: Make API coercion rules explicit
check: Review how booleans, null values, numbers, and dates are parsed consistently.
remediation: Define accepted wire types and return clear validation results.

title: Transmit timestamps with an explicit timezone
check: Review timestamp serialization and parsing between supported API clients.
remediation: Use a consistent format that carries the offset or UTC designation.

title: Return predictable success response shapes
check: Review request variants that return different structures for the same endpoint.
remediation: Use a predictable envelope or clearly documented variants.

title: Treat field removal and meaning changes as breaking
check: Compare backward-compatible additions with deletions or changed field semantics.
remediation: Use explicit versioning or migrate consumers before removing old fields.

title: Return safe support correlation references
check: Review ordinary API errors for an identifier that can locate related diagnostics.
remediation: Return a non-sensitive correlation reference and include it in restricted logs.

title: Verify webhook source before processing
check: Review webhook handlers for provider-provided verification and secret-rotation behavior.
remediation: Use the provider's supported verification library and narrowly scope configured credentials.

title: Handle duplicate webhook delivery
check: Review owned webhook fixtures for repeated delivery of the same event.
remediation: Deduplicate by the provider's stable event identity and record the decision.

title: Respect downstream rate and payload limits
check: Review integration contracts for retry guidance, concurrency limits, and payload sizes.
remediation: Honor provider limits and expose explicit recoverable errors.

title: Define what a partial integration outcome means
check: Review how upstream timeouts are handled when work may already have succeeded downstream.
remediation: Use inquiry or reconciliation where the external result is uncertain.

title: Keep external payload conversion explicit
check: Review how external fields are translated into internal domain values.
remediation: Map fields and expectations at the adapter and reject unsupported values clearly.

title: Use owned test fixtures for integrations
check: Review test configuration for endpoints, users, and credentials used in integration runs.
remediation: Use local simulators or explicitly approved sandbox endpoints with disposable fixtures.

title: Define the supported browser and device matrix
check: Review product assumptions against the browsers and device types users are expected to use.
remediation: Maintain a practical browser and device matrix and validate core journeys against it.

title: Run supported language and framework releases
check: Compare deployed and CI runtime versions with the project's supported range.
remediation: Standardize builds and deployments on maintained versions and plan upgrades.

title: Keep controls usable with the virtual keyboard
check: Review short mobile viewports while a form field is focused using an owned device fixture.
remediation: Adapt scrolling and bottom controls to the available viewport.

title: Support native form autofill consistently
check: Review the input types, names, and autocomplete tokens in common account forms.
remediation: Use platform semantics for fields and keep user-entered values usable.

title: Display numbers and dates in the selected locale
check: Review supported locale fixtures using the same known amounts and instants.
remediation: Use a locale-aware formatter and keep underlying values unambiguous.

title: Check right-to-left layout where supported
check: Review navigation, table alignment, and reading order in an available right-to-left locale.
remediation: Use direction-aware styling and verify icon meanings separately.

title: Preserve Unicode values across storage and transport
check: Review owned multilingual fixtures from form input through storage and display.
remediation: Use consistent UTF-8 and explicit normalization where comparison rules require it.

title: Make exports compatible with supported consumers
check: Review controlled imports of representative exports in supported applications.
remediation: Document the delimiter, encoding, newline handling, and date format.

title: Verify both current and preceding API clients
check: Run representative compatibility fixtures against the client versions that remain supported.
remediation: Keep server changes compatible until supported consumers have migrated.

title: Provide a fallback for optional browser features
check: Review a core journey in an owned browser fixture where an optional interface API is unavailable.
remediation: Keep essential behavior available through a supported fallback.

title: Keep core use working with optional cookies disabled
check: Review core owned journeys with optional tracking denied.
remediation: Separate required session behavior from optional analytics and preferences.

title: Handle old and new app versions during rolling deployment
check: Review request and worker behavior while adjacent releases may coexist.
remediation: Use backward-compatible writes, contracts, and rollback steps for the coexistence window.

title: Keep import and path case consistent
check: Review asset and module paths across case-sensitive and case-insensitive platforms.
remediation: Match declared file names exactly and include a Linux build check.

title: Support touch, pointer, and keyboard input
check: Review essential controls with each supported input mode.
remediation: Avoid reliance on hover-only behavior or pointer-only gesture shortcuts.

title: Verify URL generation behind the configured proxy
check: Review owned staging responses for correct host, scheme, and ports in generated links.
remediation: Configure only the trusted proxy settings required by the deployment.

title: Verify dates across daylight-saving transitions
check: Review test fixtures around local offset changes and repeated or skipped local times.
remediation: Operate on unambiguous instants and define how local schedules resolve transitions.

title: Prove the regression before changing the behavior
check: Review a focused owned test that fails against the recorded pre-fix behavior.
remediation: Create a deterministic test that fails for the intended reason and passes with the fix.

title: Verify expected outcomes beyond a successful status
check: Review a core test for meaningful assertions about persisted and visible outcomes.
remediation: Assert the user-visible result or stable contract and relevant state.

title: Cover meaningful input boundaries
check: Review tests around documented minimums, maximums, and empty input.
remediation: Use named fixtures on either side of each important boundary.

title: Test that rejected actions leave no unintended effect
check: Review rejected owned fixtures and their persisted state after the operation.
remediation: Assert both the expected rejection and the absence of side effects.

title: Make time-dependent tests deterministic
check: Review time-sensitive tests for wall-clock scheduling or arbitrary waits.
remediation: Use a controllable clock and assert state transitions after explicit time movement.

title: Make external dependencies controllable in tests
check: Review tests for reliance on variable upstream responses or live service credentials.
remediation: Use explicit fakes for external boundaries and separate authorized integration runs.

title: Exercise actual background task effects
check: Review whether a dispatch assertion is the only coverage of business work in a job.
remediation: Test the worker handler with owned state and a controlled dependency boundary.

title: Use known expected values for transformations
check: Review expected test data for values computed using the same implementation.
remediation: Use independently chosen inputs and expected values from the documented behavior.

title: Use production-like but synthetic fixture shapes
check: Review fixture ranges and relationships against the cases the application supports.
remediation: Use representative generated data without real user records.

title: Keep test setup isolated and repeatable
check: Review for dependence on test order or artifacts from preceding cases.
remediation: Create necessary state in each test and clean up shared resources.

title: Make CI failures block rollout
check: Review a controlled failing CI fixture and confirm release steps do not run.
remediation: Tie production deployment to the verified result for the same commit.

title: Report what each test run exercised
check: Review how the system distinguishes passed, skipped, unavailable, and unexecuted checks.
remediation: Report each state separately with the evidence that supports it.

title: Capture comparable screenshots for a verified fix
check: Check before and after screenshots for matching viewport, data, and journey state.
remediation: Record the setup for each image and explain meaningful differences.

title: Require review for visual baseline changes
check: Review how a deliberate baseline update is approved and stored.
remediation: Make baseline changes explicit and preserve before and after evidence.

title: Give each browser case its own state
check: Review cookies, local storage, and authentication shared across browser tests.
remediation: Use separate browser contexts or clean state for independent cases.

title: Verify a small, safe smoke suite after releases
check: Review the approved smoke checks selected for a deployed release.
remediation: Check critical read-only availability and keep mutating checks in owned test environments.

title: Use consistent structured event logs
check: Review sample logs for event names and relevant non-sensitive identifiers.
remediation: Log important outcomes with structured fields and defined severity.

title: Correlate requests across owned services
check: Review traces and logs for a stable request or trace identifier across service boundaries.
remediation: Propagate a defined correlation context through supported telemetry libraries.

title: Correlate background jobs with their origin
check: Review whether a queued task can be traced back to its initiating operation.
remediation: Pass safe correlation context through dispatch and record the job identity at execution.

title: Preserve trace relationships across integrations
check: Review a representative owned trace for missing spans or disconnected services.
remediation: Propagate standard trace context and name spans by operation.

title: Choose sampling that preserves important signals
check: Review sampling settings for how error, critical, and high-volume paths are represented.
remediation: Document the sampling policy and preserve enough failure evidence for diagnostics.

title: Keep metric labels bounded
check: Review metric dimensions for request IDs, raw URLs, or user identifiers.
remediation: Use low-cardinality dimensions for metrics and use restricted tracing for details.

title: Measure completed user journeys
check: Review health dashboards for signals tied to user-visible success and failure.
remediation: Record outcome metrics for critical actions and relate them to availability targets.

title: Route actionable alerts to an owner
check: Review a sample alert for severity, ownership, and a practical response path.
remediation: Assign on-call ownership and include the relevant runbook.

title: Reduce duplicate or unactionable alerts
check: Review recent alert episodes for duplicate pages and alerts with no response action.
remediation: Aggregate related conditions and tune thresholds to the agreed reliability goals.

title: Watch backlog age as well as size
check: Review dispatch and worker telemetry for age of unfinished work.
remediation: Record oldest job age and queue depth with a threshold based on user impact.

title: Annotate telemetry with release identity
check: Review metrics and traces around a deployment for an unambiguous revision marker.
remediation: Attach the release identity and deployment timestamp to relevant observability signals.

title: Keep private values out of diagnostic logs
check: Review log capture and serializer boundaries for credentials, personal fields, and raw request bodies.
remediation: Redact fields centrally and verify the resulting output with a synthetic fixture.

title: Apply retention to logs and traces
check: Review retention, access, and deletion settings for each diagnostic store.
remediation: Set a purpose-appropriate retention period and protect access to retained diagnostics.

title: Expose when telemetry is unavailable
check: Review whether missing telemetry is distinguishable from a healthy workload.
remediation: Monitor ingestion and alert delivery and display gaps or stale samples explicitly.

title: Show next steps with status indicators
check: Review a production dashboard for clear thresholds, freshness, and a path to diagnosis.
remediation: Connect status to an owner, time window, and relevant trace or runbook.

title: Preserve investigation context when reporting exceptions
check: Review error handling for enough sanitized context to distinguish where a failure originated.
remediation: Record safe operation identifiers and preserve the original exception chain.

title: Identify personal data in the workflow
check: Review which personal fields are collected, stored, shared, or deleted in the feature.
remediation: Maintain a data-flow map with data owners and intended purposes.

title: Collect data required for the intended purpose
check: Review each required field for a documented purpose and decision it enables.
remediation: Remove unnecessary fields and make optional fields honestly optional.

title: Keep secondary data use explicit
check: Review whether collected data is reused beyond the original feature purpose.
remediation: Document and authorize distinct uses separately where applicable.

title: Set retention by data purpose
check: Review whether different records and evidence types have appropriate retention rules.
remediation: Apply and monitor retention policies that fit each use case.

title: Verify individual data deletion using synthetic records
check: Review what happens to related records, cached entries, exports, and background work after a controlled deletion.
remediation: Define deletion behavior for each store and check it with an authorized fixture.

title: Scope exports to the authorized subject
check: Review export queries and download routes for ownership and expiry checks.
remediation: Apply the same authorization and evidence limits when preparing and serving an export.

title: Keep personal records out of test fixtures
check: Review test fixture sources, screenshots, and seed data for real personal information.
remediation: Generate synthetic fixtures that preserve useful structure without personal details.

title: Review the contents captured in UI evidence
check: Check which fields or views can appear in automatically collected screenshots.
remediation: Mask sensitive form areas and restrict evidence access by user and retention period.

title: Keep support data access accountable
check: Review which support actions can display customer information and how access is recorded.
remediation: Keep privileges scoped and log access events with a clear operational owner.

title: Apply privacy controls to copied data
check: Review backups and replicated datasets for access control, encryption, and retention.
remediation: Use least-privilege access and apply policy to each retained copy.

title: Know what leaves the application boundary
check: Review integrations for the data fields and recipients involved.
remediation: Limit transmitted fields to the documented purpose and review downstream handling.

title: Honor the user's analytics preference
check: Review whether optional telemetry starts before consent or continues after the user changes their preference.
remediation: Gate analytics at the appropriate preference boundary and honor changes promptly.

title: Explain data choices in context
check: Review requests for personal information for a plain explanation of what is needed and why.
remediation: Use specific text close to the relevant field or choice.

title: Maintain a record of data processing locations
check: Review where primary stores, backups, and third-party processors operate.
remediation: Record relevant regions and keep the data-processing inventory current.

title: Propagate corrections to dependent records
check: Review correction workflows for derivative records that preserve stale values unintentionally.
remediation: Update supported dependent copies or document how consistency is restored.

title: Restrict the audience for privacy-related logs
check: Review access to audit or telemetry stores that contain personal identifiers.
remediation: Limit access to authorized roles and apply short retention where appropriate.

title: Identify the source behind each deployed artifact
check: Review whether deployed images or bundles can be traced to a verified source revision.
remediation: Record the commit, artifact identifier, and verification result for each deployment.

title: Build from resolved dependencies
check: Review build manifests and lockfiles for reproducible dependency resolution.
remediation: Prefer locked dependencies and document any required non-reproducible step.

title: Keep environment-specific credentials outside the build
check: Review image builds and deployment pipeline inputs for embedded environment values.
remediation: Use a runtime secret mechanism and pass only non-sensitive build configuration during build.

title: Verify readiness before declaring deployment success
check: Review post-deploy checks for whether core application availability is measured.
remediation: Require readiness and safe smoke evidence before marking a rollout complete.

title: Keep simultaneous releases from racing
check: Review workflow and deploy scripts for competing updates to the same environment.
remediation: Serialize environment deployments and reject superseded release requests.

title: Run migrations in an intentional release phase
check: Review migration timing against the compatibility requirements of old and new versions.
remediation: Define the deployment order and use staged schema changes when releases may overlap.

title: Keep a rollback plan for each release
check: Review whether the last healthy artifact and data compatibility are known.
remediation: Record a reversible deployment path and rehearse recovery on an owned environment.

title: Limit exposure while validating risky changes
check: Review how a rollout can be stopped after early signals show a problem.
remediation: Use staged exposure with objective health goals and a defined stop condition.

title: Document how deployment settings are initialized
check: Review how a new environment gets defaults while preserving operator-provided values.
remediation: Use a versioned safe configuration template and fill secrets through a private channel.

title: Record who requested and approved a deployment
check: Review release records for the human or workload identity behind each action.
remediation: Persist an audit event with the actor, environment, revision, and outcome.

title: Keep production access out of pull request jobs
check: Review CI event triggers and deployment credential permissions.
remediation: Run validation with limited access and expose deployment identity only to protected release jobs.

title: Set clear build and deployment time limits
check: Review whether stalled pipeline steps can block later releases indefinitely.
remediation: Set reasonable timeouts and surface the stage at which an attempt stopped.

title: Keep dependency caches tied to the build inputs
check: Review artifact caches for runtime version and dependency lockfile inputs.
remediation: Use cache keys that reflect the exact dependency and runtime requirements.

title: Pin automation dependencies to reviewed versions
check: Review CI actions, tools, and build base images for the expected version-control policy.
remediation: Use reviewed pins and update them through a regular maintenance path.

title: Keep release notes tied to the changes delivered
check: Review release notes for behavior changes, compatibility impact, and operator steps.
remediation: Record relevant changes with the release and avoid exposing private implementation data.

title: Track meaningful staging and production differences
check: Review deployment settings for differences that affect smoke tests, migrations, or performance.
remediation: Keep essential runtime behavior aligned and document intentional environment differences.
